Not really, Greece can easily accept the terms of the bailouts and preserve the Eurozone. Furthermore that fraternity that exists has been betrayed by Greece. How do you think the small eastern European countries feel in this situation? They (think Poland maybe) contributed money to the bailout, despite the fact that really can't spare it, on good faith that Greece would work out a way to pay it back. Now Greece is not working that way out.

It is likely (although by no means certain) that Wolfgang Schäuble, Merkel’s hardline finance minister, is right when he suggests that a Greek exit from the euro zone, even a disorderly one, would not have a major economic impact on the rest of Europe.

This is true, as I said before. They key is to then work out a political mechanism to determine how one leaves more orderly next time, and how can one return.

I think the main focus of this crisis should be what happens with Greece after they miss the July 20th payment and Exit. How can Europe help create a stable government and help Greece transition back to the Drachma. The exit will have much larger consequences for Greece than the rest of Europe.
